title: A universal gauge structure in the photon content of light-matter systems
abstract: After truncating the matter Hilbert space of a single-mode light-matter model, gauge transformations leave the spectrum invariant whereas the ground-state photon number is gauge dependent, hence, its meaning remains disputed. We show that this gauge dependence obeys an exact algebraic law whenever the gauge transformation acts as a displacement of the field coupled to a matter operator $G$. Namely, the ground-state photon number is a quadratic polynomial in the gauge parameter $λ$, $\langle a^{\dagger} a\rangle_λ$ $=$ $\langle a^{\dagger} a\rangle_{0}$ $+$ $Cλ$ $+$ $Qλ^2$. Here the coefficients are the correlator $C=\langle G\,p\rangle$ of $G$ and the field momentum $p$, and $Q=\langle G^2\rangle$. Its minimum over all gauges is naturally gauge-invariant, and for the quantum Rabi model it is determined by the ground-state energy alone. We show that it is strictly positive for the quantum Rabi and Dicke models with level splitting, so that a residual photon content survives in every gauge. At weak coupling the gauge of minimal photon number is the Jaynes-Cummings gauge, and for the Dicke model it remains so at all couplings in the thermodynamic limit.
summary: This paper analyzes the gauge dependence of the ground-state photon number in light-matter systems like the QRM and Dicke model. It proves that this dependence is quadratic in the gauge parameter, leading to a unique, gauge-invariant minimum photon number. This minimum is shown to be strictly positive, indicating a residual, physically meaningful photon content even when the system is strongly coupled.
main_problem: The paper investigates the gauge dependence of the ground-state photon number in light-matter systems after truncating the matter Hilbert space.
main_result: The ground-state photon number follows an exact quadratic law in the gauge parameter, and its minimum value across all gauges is gauge-invariant and strictly positive for models like the QRM and Dicke model.
method: The analysis uses unitary gauge transformations parameterized by $\lambda$ to transform field operators and calculate the expectation value $\langle a^\dagger a angle_\lambda$ exactly.
model_or_system: The study focuses on single-mode light-matter models, specifically the Quantum Rabi Model (QRM) and the Dicke model, involving coupling between a single cavity mode and a matter system.
key_observables: Ground-state photon number ($\langle a^\dagger a angle_\lambda$), minimum photon number ($\langle a^\dagger a angle_{\min}$), and the coefficients $C$ and $Q$ defining the quadratic dependence.
important_parameters: The gauge parameter $\lambda$, coupling strengths, and the level splitting of the matter system are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the gauge transformation acts as a displacement of the field coupled to a matter operator $G$, and it relies on truncating the matter Hilbert space.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the gauge family of the photon dressing, showing the invariance of the position quadrature and the parabolic dependence of $\langle p^2 angle_\lambda$ and $\langle a^\dagger a angle_\lambda$ on $\lambda$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the quadratic dependence of $\langle a^\dagger a angle_\lambda$ on $\lambda$, derives the gauge-invariant minimum, and then applies this framework to the QRM and Dicke models to show the physical implications regarding residual photon content and superradiance.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for handling gauge ambiguities in open quantum systems, which is crucial for correctly identifying physical observables in cavity QED and light-matter interactions.

figures.caption: Figure 1: The gauge family of the photon dressing. Changing the gauge param- eter λ in Uλ = exp[iλG(a + a†)] leaves the position quadrature x of the field unchanged and both shifts and reshapes the momentum quadrature p. The top row shows phase-space insets from the Coulomb gauge (left), through λ∗, to the dipole gauge (right). The momentum fluctuation ⟨p2⟩λ is itself a parabola in λ, narrowest at λ∗. The ground-state photon number ⟨a†a⟩λ follows the matching exact parabola (bottom), and its minimum at λ∗is strictly positive and the same in every gauge, corresponding to the photon dressing that no gauge choice re- moves (Sec. 2).

Figure 2: Validity of the truncated tunable-coherent-state expansion for ∆= 0.7, Π = 1, g = 0.8. (a) Convergence of the coherent-state parameter ξ with the truncation N. (b) Coefficient magnitudes |cn| for N = 8, 12, 16, 24 (markers, shown only up to n = N), which fall on the converged curve (line) and reach about 10−25 at N = 24. (c) ln |cn| against ln n! is linear with slope ≈−0.96, so |cn| ∼(n!)−0.96, a decay faster than any geometric rate. The displacement ξ obtained from the truncation condition cN+1(ξ) = 0 converges quickly with N, so a short truncation already gives a numerically exact approximation of the Rabi wavefunctions.

Figure 3: Ground-state photon number of the standard Rabi model (10), which equals that in the dipole gauge, versus coupling g, from exact diagonalization (Ncutoff = 160, ωc = 1), for three detunings ∆= 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 ωc. The curves grow monotonically as the counter-rotating terms dress the ground state. The Jaynes- Cummings counterpart at ∆= 0.7 ωc stays at zero, because its ground state decouples exactly from the coupling for g < √2ωc∆≈1.18 ωc. The two mod- els therefore separate strongly once the counter-rotating terms matter, which is where the gauge question becomes consequential. (c) Photon number versus α for several g (dots mark the minima), following the fixed-curvature parabola of (26). (d) Minimal photon number ⟨a†a⟩min versus g, reached at αmin = C/2η.

The photon number is an exact parabola in the gauge parameter for every Ns, and (4) matches the numerics to machine precision. (b) Curvature Q = ⟨G2⟩versus coupling, for the gauge-invariant model (solid) and the standard model (dashed). Q is an ordinary ground-state moment and is well defined for either Hamiltonian.
